text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Wednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Kazimieras Skeberdis, a road traffic policeman, confessed to stabbing his wife, Laima Skeberdiene, who was secretary of the ministry of government reform and municipal affairs.
- Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius asked the state security department to investigate publications that promote racism, anti-semitism and xenophobic ideas.
- Lithuania offered to help Germany deal with the flood of the Oder river by sending a helicopter and 15 volunteers.
- The government decided to increase the share capital of Savings Bank by 20 million litas, from its current 60 million litas, through a share issue.
- Lithuania's largest paper manufacturer Grigishkes has decreased its foreign capital 32 percent to 15 percent by buying back shares on the stock exchange in recent months.
- Knitwear manufacturer Utena Trikotazas increased its exports by 15 percent this year, selling 26.5 million litas worth of goods abroad.
- Over 3,000 enterprises were liquidated in the first half of 1997.
- Hanza Lizingas, the Lithuanan subsidiary of Estonia's Hansa Leasing Group, reported a 503,000 litas profit for the first half of 1997.
- The state securities commission will this month decide on a seven million litas share issue by Snoras bank.

- Lithuanian Railways had a net profit of 2.2 million litas in the first half of 1997 versus a loss of five million litas in the same period last year. The company said it hauled 12 percent more cargo after reducing fees.
- Former leader of pro-Soviet group Yedinstvo, Valerii Ivanov, appealed a sentence of jail for one year for slander.
- Polish Economy Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek will arrive in Vilnius for a two-day working visit, during which he will meet with Vagnorius Economy Minister Vincas Babilius.
- Lithuania signed a deal to make Union Bank of Switzerland the advisor in the privatisation of Lithuanian Telecom.
- The privatisation commission approved the privatisation programmes for stevedoring company Klaipedos Smelte and Anapole, which installs and mounts oil processing equipment, for September.
